content:
Evolutionary Campaign Evolutionary campaign mode coordinates bounded multi-generation optimization over mutable EVOLVE-BLOCK source regions, isolated child LocalRunStore runs, and hardware-verified benchmark-gate.v1 receipts. Loopwright maintains a fenced campaign.sqlite Pareto archive and exports signed evolution-bundle.v1 packages without delegating verification authority to models.
For single-run repository automation, follow Declarative Taskpack . For manual out-of-repo controller governance, follow Managed Controller .
Contents Overview Prompt bootstrap Step 1: Mark evolve blocks Step 2: Author taskpack Step 3: Author campaign Step 4: Start runner Step 5: Run and export Overview Evolutionary campaign mode separates candidate authoring from blind hardware evaluation across three zones:
Responsibility Authored files Runtime invariant Mutable span guard EVOLVE-BLOCK markers and evolve-block-guard.v1 Outside bytes must match baseline SHA-256 exactly Hardware contract target.matrix[].hardware and benchmark-gate.v1 Stage A static audit blocks forbidden symbols and excess spills Blind evaluation Outbound runner relay and runner worker Zero inbound GPU cluster ports; offline Stage B holdout data Archive and export .loopwright/campaign.yaml and loopwright evolve Fenced campaign.sqlite outside --repo; signed HMAC export Prompt bootstrap To configure an evolutionary campaign through an interview-first flow before writing YAML files, paste this prompt into your coding agent inside the target repository:
textCopy Read https://docs.gpustack.ai/loopwright/llms.txt and its Bootstrap Interview Reference (https://docs.gpustack.ai/loopwright/references/bootstrap-interview.md). Inspect this repository first WITHOUT editing any files yet, then follow Evolutionary campaign mode (Mode 3) to interview me one question at a time with repository-grounded defaults on EVOLVE-BLOCK guarded files, target hardware cell and Stage A static audit limits, held-out benchmark-gate.v1 workloads and runner relay/worker topology, objectives, island/niche budgets, optional teamEvolution, and bundle export. Wait for my approval on the design summary before generating .loopwright/taskpack.yaml and .loopwright/campaign.yaml and validating with loopwright evolve check. Step 1: Mark evolve blocks Wrap only editable spans in guarded source files with matching EVOLVE-BLOCK-START: <id> and EVOLVE-BLOCK-END: <id> comments (//, #, or /* */):
cppCopy __global__ void flash_decode(float* out, const float* q, int n) { // EVOLVE-BLOCK-START: tile_loop for (int i = threadIdx.x; i < n; i += blockDim.x) { out[i] = q[i]; } // EVOLVE-BLOCK-END: tile_loop } Keep block IDs unique per file and bounded to printable ASCII. Any byte change outside marked spans fails evolve-block-guard.v1 before hardware dispatch.
Step 2: Author taskpack Create .loopwright/taskpack.yaml declaring guarded files, the hardware target cell, Stage A static audit ceilings, and benchmark-gate.v1 (see Taskpack and Task Contract ):
yamlCopy apiVersion: loopwright.dev/v1alpha1 kind: Taskpack metadata: name: kernel-evolve-tp spec: goal: candidate: Optimize guarded kernel blocks and pass hardware benchmark thresholds. noChange: Confirm no further optimization is needed and settle cleanly. target: matrix: - id: cuda-h100-whole platform: linux/amd64 variant: cuda12 hardware: accelerator: sm_90a isolationMode: whole_device deviceCount: 1 driverConstraint: ">=550.0" forbiddenSymbolPatterns: - cublas - cudnn maxRegisterCount: 128 # Optional maxLocalSpillBytes: 0 # Optional scope: writable: - src/kernels/** protected: - .loopwright/** - scripts/** models: - provider: openai id: gpt-5 apiKeyEnv: LOOPWRIGHT_PROVIDER_TOKEN roles: - id: mutator provider: openai model: gpt-5 purpose: task tools: - read - write - edit prompt: Edit guarded EVOLVE-BLOCK spans in src/kernels/flash_decode.cu only. verification: localChecks: - id: evolve-guard implementation: evolve-block-guard.v1 parameters: files: - src/kernels/flash_decode.cu allowedBlockIds: # Optional - tile_loop maxBlockBytes: 8192 # Optional externalGates: - id: gpu-bench implementation: benchmark-gate.v1 endpointId: hw-relay gateId: flash-decode-bench required: true targetCellId: cuda-h100-whole heldOutWorkloadId: decode-bs1-4k metricThresholds: - kind: bounds metric: max_ulp max: 2 bucketScope: all_buckets publication: mode: disabled Step 3: Author campaign Create .loopwright/campaign.yaml referencing the taskpack and target cell (see Evolution Campaign ):
yamlCopy apiVersion: loopwright.dev/v1alpha1 kind: EvolutionCampaign metadata: name: flash-decode-sm90a spec: taskpack: .loopwright/taskpack.yaml targetCellId: cuda-h100-whole tracks: # Optional - triton - cute - cuda_raw stages: # Optional mode: single-target # Optional population: islands: 2 migrationIntervalGenerations: 6 maxMigrationElites: 1 nicheAxes: - id: bound_pipeline kind: enum values: - hbm - l2 - smem_lds_ub - tensor_cube - vector_valu sampling: noveltyDecayLambda: 1.0 mutationWeights: diff_tune: 0.5 full_rewrite: 0.3 crossover: 0.2 modelBandit: deterministic-round-robin # Optional maxCrossoversPerPrompt: 2 objectives: - metric: latency_us_p50 direction: minimize - metric: goodput_rps direction: maximize budgets: maxGenerations: 20 maxEvaluations: 40 maxConcurrentEvaluations: 2 scratchpadIntervalGenerations: 5 # Optional export: # Optional format: oci-layout # Optional outputDir: .loopwright-out/bundles/flash-decode-sm90a Validate both manifests and guarded files offline before starting any worker:
shCopy loopwright evolve check --campaign .loopwright/campaign.yaml --repo . --json Step 4: Start runner Start the relay in a reachable DMZ or loopback host, then start outbound workers on private GPU hosts:
shCopy loopwright runner relay --config "$HOME/loopwright-ops/relay.yaml" --json loopwright runner worker --config "$HOME/loopwright-ops/worker.yaml" --json For offline smoke tests without GPUs, set probeMode: synthetic_fixture on the worker and pass --allow-synthetic-probe to evolve run. Omit --allow-synthetic-probe on real hardware so synthetic receipts fail closed (HARDWARE_PROVENANCE_MISMATCH).
Step 5: Run and export Export required secrets and point --state strictly outside --repo:
shCopy export LOOPWRIGHT_PROVIDER_TOKEN="<provider-token>" export LOOPWRIGHT_BENCHMARK_GATE_URL="https://relay.example.internal/v1/benchmark/jobs" export LOOPWRIGHT_GATE_SIGNING_SECRET="<hmac-secret>" loopwright evolve run --campaign .loopwright/campaign.yaml --state "$HOME/evo-state/flash-decode" --repo . --json Monitor progress, pause cleanly on SIGINT (exit 130), resume later, and export signed evolution-bundle.v1 packages (EXPORT_UNVERIFIED_FORBIDDEN, exit 3 when receipts or secrets are unverified):
shCopy loopwright evolve status --campaign "$HOME/evo-state/flash-decode" --json loopwright evolve inspect --campaign "$HOME/evo-state/flash-decode" --island 0 --json loopwright evolve resume --campaign "$HOME/evo-state/flash-decode" --repo . --json loopwright evolve export --campaign "$HOME/evo-state/flash-decode" --out "$HOME/evo-out/bundle" --format oci-layout --json See also — Evolution Campaign (EvolutionCampaign schema and bundle contract) · CLI (runner and evolve subcommands) · Taskpack (evolve-block-guard.v1 and benchmark-gate.v1 declarations)

content:
Managed Controller Managed controller mode is Loopwright’s fine-grained governance workflow for platform engineers and local CLI operators. Author an out-of-repo TrustedRegistry, pin its SHA-256 digest inside ControllerConfig alongside a TaskContract DAG, and drive runs via the loopwright CLI.
For single-file repository automation where Loopwright compiles contracts and digests automatically, follow Declarative Taskpack instead.
Contents Configuration relationships Overview Prompt bootstrap Step 1: Generate drafts Step 2: Pin registry Step 3: Author controller Step 4: Execute run Step 5: Reconcile receipts Configuration relationships Managed controller mode coordinates an operator-owned authority store (TrustedRegistry) with a run configuration (ControllerConfig embedding TaskContract):

To assemble tailored registry.yaml and controller.yaml files interactively without looking up digests by hand, paste this prompt into your coding agent:
textCopy Read https://docs.gpustack.ai/loopwright/llms.txt and its Bootstrap Interview Reference (https://docs.gpustack.ai/loopwright/references/bootstrap-interview.md). Inspect this repository first WITHOUT editing any files yet, then interview me one question at a time with repository-grounded defaults to align on writable/protected scope, budgets, verification checks, and role bindings. Wait for my approval on the design summary before computing local Loopwright handler and graph SHA-256 digests, writing out-of-repo registry.yaml and controller.yaml, and validating with loopwright check. Step 1: Generate drafts Install @gpustack/loopwright (see Installation ) and initialize starter YAML files in real non-symlink directories outside the target repository:
shCopy mkdir -p "$HOME/loopwright-ops" "$HOME/loopwright-runs" "$HOME/loopwright-trust" loopwright init --directory "$HOME/loopwright-ops" cp "$HOME/loopwright-ops/registry.draft.yaml" "$HOME/loopwright-trust/registry.yaml" cp "$HOME/loopwright-ops/controller.draft.yaml" "$HOME/loopwright-ops/controller.yaml" Keep registry.yaml (0600) in $HOME/loopwright-trust outside cwd, outside $HOME/loopwright-ops, and outside any target repository (REGISTRY_UNTRUSTED).
Step 2: Pin registry Compute installed handler and runtime digests from your Loopwright installation so registry.yaml pins verified code bytes:
shCopy node --input-type=module -e " import { createHash } from 'node:crypto'; import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs'; import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url'; import { installedHandlerDigests } from '@loopwright/controller'; import { describePiAdapterFiles } from '@loopwright/agent-pi'; const handlers = await installedHandlerDigests(); const pi = await describePiAdapterFiles(); const lock = readFileSync(fileURLToPath(new URL('../../../package-lock.json', import.meta.resolve('@loopwright/agent-pi')))); console.log({ handlers, pi, graphSha256: createHash('sha256').update(lock).digest('hex') }); " Populate $HOME/loopwright-trust/registry.yaml (see Controller and Registry for every field in roleProfiles, runtimeProfiles, mcp, and endpoints):
yamlCopy apiVersion: loopwright.dev/v1alpha1 kind: TrustedRegistry metadata: name: prod-operator-registry spec: version: 1 resourceVersion: rev-2026-11 handlers: - id: pi-author version: 1 kind: agent implementation: pi.agent.v1 digest: algorithm: sha256 hex: <hash> parameters: prompt: Update packages/app/manifest.json. purpose: task capabilities: - pi - id: check-manifest-json version: 1 kind: check implementation: json-artifact.v1 digest: algorithm: sha256 hex: <hash> parameters: checkId: manifest-json path: packages/app/manifest.json required: - schema_version equals: schema_version: 1 capabilities: - inert_bytes - read_only roleProfiles: - id: builder-profile selection: provider: zai model: glm-5.3 thinking: high api: openai-completions tools: - read - write - edit context: mode: proven_bound estimator: lw-pi-final-json-bytes-v1 proofId: null version: 1 evidence: estimated workingWindowCeiling: 98304 maxRequestBytes: 65536 serviceMargin: 32768 toolReserve: 16384 maxOutputTokens: 1024 runtimeRef: default-runtime providerCredentialRef: zai-token mcp: serverId: workspace scriptDigest: algorithm: sha256 hex: <hash> names: [] effects: [] idleTimeoutSeconds: 2 absoluteTimeoutSeconds: 10 resources: [] runtimeProfiles: - id: default-runtime dockerExecutable: /usr/local/bin/docker dockerSocket: /var/run/docker.sock identity: sdkIntegrity: <sdk-integrity> graphDigest: algorithm: sha256 hex: <hash> imageDigest: sha256:<hash> configDigest: algorithm: sha256 hex: <hash> profile: linux/arm64 credentialBindings: - id: zai-token consumer: provider destinationRef: zai environmentNames: - ZAI_API_KEY template: "${ZAI_API_KEY}" environmentBindings: - name: ZAI_API_KEY classification: credential paths: - /spec/credentials/0/template Compute the SHA-256 digest of the finalized registry.yaml:
shCopy REGISTRY_SHA=$(shasum -a 256 "$HOME/loopwright-trust/registry.yaml" | awk '{print $1}') Step 3: Author controller Edit $HOME/loopwright-ops/controller.yaml to embed your TaskContract, bind registry.name + $REGISTRY_SHA, and map roles and steps (see Task Contract for all contract fields):
yamlCopy apiVersion: loopwright.dev/v1alpha1 kind: ControllerConfig spec: registry: name: prod-operator-registry digest: algorithm: sha256 hex: <hash> task: apiVersion: loopwright.dev/v1alpha1 kind: TaskContract spec: goal: Update packages/app/manifest.json release metadata and pass JSON validation. taskpack: app-manifest target: repository: acme/example-app baseRevision: main sourceRevision: v1.4.0 matrix: null scope: writable: - "packages/app/**" protected: - "packages/app/policy/**" roles: - id: builder adapter: pi provider: zai model: glm-5.3 thinking: high tools: - read - write - edit trustedContext: revision: rev-2026-11 discovery: disabled resources: [] budgets: wallTimeMs: 300000 # Must exceed controls.drainReserveMs (120000 ms). totalTokens: 64000 perCallOutputTokens: 1024 maxModelCalls: 8 maxConcurrency: 1 maxFormatRepairs: 1 maxImplementationRepairs: 2 maxTransportRetries: 1 enforcement: wallTime: hard_admission tokens: soft_accounting modelCalls: hard_admission concurrency: hard_admission formatRepairs: hard_admission implementationRepairs: hard_admission transportRetries: hard_admission steps: - id: author-change kind: agent uses: pi-author roleId: builder dependsOn: [] - id: verify-manifest kind: check uses: check-manifest-json roleId: null dependsOn: - author-change acceptance: required: - manifest-json checks: - id: manifest-json allowedEvidenceLevels: - local_execution profiles: roles: - roleId: builder profileRef: builder-profile steps: - stepId: author-change handlerRef: pi-author - stepId: verify-manifest handlerRef: check-manifest-json credentials: - ref: zai-token template: "${ZAI_API_KEY}" controls: drainReserveMs: 120000 maxAttempts: 4 repeatFailureLimit: 2 submission: mode: artifact_or_assistant path: null publication: mode: disabled Step 4: Execute run Compile statically first (check makes zero network or state calls), then launch the fenced run outside $HOME/loopwright-trust:
shCopy export ZAI_API_KEY="zai_example_token" loopwright check --config "$HOME/loopwright-ops/controller.yaml" --registry "$HOME/loopwright-trust/registry.yaml" --registry-sha256 "$REGISTRY_SHA" --json loopwright run --config "$HOME/loopwright-ops/controller.yaml" --registry "$HOME/loopwright-trust/registry.yaml" --registry-sha256 "$REGISTRY_SHA" --repo /path/to/example-app --run-root "$HOME/loopwright-runs" --run-id run-20261112-01 --json Delegated execution For zero-secret delegated stepping, set adapter: delegated on the role profile (runtimeRef: null, providerCredentialRef: null, mcp: null) and task role (see Controller and Registry and CLI ):
shCopy loopwright step next --config "$HOME/loopwright-ops/controller.yaml" --registry "$HOME/loopwright-trust/registry.yaml" --registry-sha256 "$REGISTRY_SHA" --repo /path/to/example-app --run-root "$HOME/loopwright-runs" --run-id delegated-1 --role-model builder=example/author-model:medium --json loopwright step submit --run-root "$HOME/loopwright-runs" --run-id delegated-1 --lease TOKEN --status completed --json Step 5: Reconcile receipts Inspect run state and export evidence bundles offline:
shCopy loopwright status --run-root "$HOME/loopwright-runs" --run-id run-20261112-01 --json loopwright inspect --run-root "$HOME/loopwright-runs" --run-id run-20261112-01 --output "$HOME/loopwright-runs/bundle-01" Resume after restart: Run loopwright resume with the exact same config, registry, digest, repo, and run identity. content:
Documentation Loopwright supports two operating modes sharing one verification kernel: Declarative Taskpack (single-file automated repository sync via GitHub Action or App) and Managed Controller (fine-grained out-of-repo TrustedRegistry and TaskContract governance via the CLI).
Getting Started Architecture explains the four-stage execution chain, the two operating modes, and the runtime baseline. Installation installs @gpustack/loopwright, wires GitHub Actions, and provides llms.txt bootstrap prompts. Operations GitHub Action configures the reusable Action and secret bindings in workflows. GitHub App deploys the webhook and token-brokering control plane. CLI runs local compilation, execution, inspection, reconciliation, and closure audits. Coding Agents drives zero-secret delegated loopwright step loops from OAuth coding agents. Walkthroughs Declarative Taskpack walks through simple single-file repository automation and automatic synchronized workflow migration. Managed Controller walks through fine-grained out-of-repo TrustedRegistry, ControllerConfig, and CLI execution. Evolutionary Campaign coordinates multi-island evolutionary search, hardware benchmark relays, and reproducible bundle export. Configuration Taskpack documents every field and enum in .loopwright/taskpack.yaml (Taskpack) and .loopwright/suite.yaml (TaskpackSuite). Task Contract documents every field, budget, step, and evidence tier in TaskContract. Controller and Registry documents every handler, profile, credential, endpoint, and control in TrustedRegistry and ControllerConfig. Sandbox Backends covers native OS and container sandbox policies and capabilities. Decision Routing details System-One advisory confidence zones, providers, and disclosure policies. Evolution Campaign configures islands, specialist-to-portfolio stages, team evolution, and bundle export in campaign.yaml (EvolutionCampaign).
